llm.summary: The skill's purpose (a cross‑IDE skill manager) is plausible, but the runtime instructions are vague and allow the agent to fetch and run code from a third‑party GitHub repository while declaring no credentials — a mismatch that warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims cross‑IDE management, cloud sync, dynamic loading and batch installs — capabilities that normally require access to external services (GitHub, agent/IDE tokens). Yet the metadata declares no required credentials or config paths. That mismatch suggests the declared requirements are incomplete or the skill expects to obtain credentials at runtime, which is concerning.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to 'pull the engine' from a GitHub repo and to initiate installation on another assistant. The instructions are high‑level and grant broad discretion to fetch and run external code; they do not constrain what will be fetched, whether it will be executed, or whether/when credentials are requested. The document does not read local files or env vars, but its open‑ended network behavior is risky.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec; instead the guide points to an arbitrary GitHub repository (https://github.com/lanyijianke/AnySkill). GitHub is a standard host, but pulling and executing code from an unverified repo is higher risk than an instruction‑only skill that performs no network fetches. The instructions do not specify releases, checksums, or install boundaries.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No env vars or primary credential are declared, but the stated features (cross‑IDE sync, dynamic loading) would reasonably require tokens/keys for GitHub and the target IDEs/agents. The absence of declared credentials is an incoherence: either the skill is incomplete or it intends to request credentials interactively, which increases risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request system config changes in its SKILL.md. Autonomous invocation is allowed by platform default (disable-model-invocation is false) which is expected; there is no explicit attempt to persistently alter other skills or global agent settings in the provided instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill asks the assistant to fetch and 'install' code from an external GitHub repo but doesn't declare the credentials or exact install steps required. Before installing: (1) review the referenced repository yourself — read the README, inspect code and install scripts, and check recent commits/owner reputation; (2) prefer repositories with signed releases or checksums; (3) never provide high‑privilege keys (cloud or agent/IDE tokens) until you know exactly which scopes are required — use least‑privilege tokens or temporary tokens; (4) run any untrusted install inside an isolated environment (VM/container) first; (5) ask the developer for a clear install manifest describing what will be downloaded/executed and what credentials are needed. These precautions reduce the risk from vague instructions that permit arbitrary code execution.
